title: Consecutive primes alternating between 1 and 3 mod 4
credit: QED original (archived Nov 2026, restored after re-review).
plain: Prime numbers other than 2 leave remainder 1 or 3 when divided by 4. Shiu proved that arbitrarily long runs of consecutive primes all with the same remainder occur. Show that, for every k, there are infinitely many runs of k consecutive primes whose remainders alternate 1, 3, 1, 3, .... Even k = 3 (a prime that is 3 mod 4 sandwiched between two primes that are 1 mod 4) is open.
math: Let $p_n$ be the $n$-th prime. Prove that for every $k\ge3$ there are infinitely many $n$ with $p_{n+i}\equiv 2-(-1)^{i}\pmod 4$ for $0\le i<k$ (i.e. the residues run $1,3,1,3,\dots$). The first open case is $k=3$: infinitely many $n$ with $(p_n,p_{n+1},p_{n+2})\equiv(1,3,1)\pmod 4$.
